# Hush

> Hush is a privacy-first web app by AQERIONX for encrypting a note and carrying it with an emoji message or PNG image.

## Website

- Homepage: https://hush.aqerionx.in/
- Public source code and project documentation: https://github.com/monu-2008/hush

## How it works

Hush encrypts notes in the browser with AES-256-GCM. It derives a key from the user's password using PBKDF2-SHA-256. The user can copy an emoji message containing invisible encrypted characters or download a PNG container. A recipient provides the complete emoji message or original PNG and the separately shared password to decrypt it in their own browser.

## Privacy and limitations

- Messages, passwords, and chosen images are processed locally and are not uploaded to a Hush backend.
- Hush does not have a server-side account system, database, or message recovery process.
- Some messaging apps remove invisible Unicode characters or recompress images. Send a test first; for images, send the original PNG as a file or document.
- The PNG carrier stores encrypted data in a PNG chunk. It is a container format, not pixel-level steganography; the presence of an encrypted payload can be discovered, but its contents require the password.
- A forgotten password cannot be recovered.

## Project documentation

See the GitHub README for the academic-project overview, architecture, cryptography choices, local setup, tests, deployment notes, and known limitations.
